answer.rationale: Memory c2 already reports that the low-cost vendor's unit cost was sharply lower and that onboarding plus invoice accuracy were unproblematic; pulling it verifies that nothing in the original record contradicts the summary. Memory c1 confirms that staying with the incumbent carried no integration cost, which is the real alternative cost I'd give up by switching. The 18% mandate is met by the low-cost quote alone, and because the assembly line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, I would not add a second source this cycle; doing so would spend the single decision slot without meeting the finance mandate. Negotiation or deferral does not meet the hard deadline in 14 days, and neither has a recorded basis for producing the required 18% cut. If the archive records support c2, I will issue a short initial term with clear performance gates before full volume transition, so that the switch does not become locked in if delivery performance deteriorates.
